items.t: Urge state emergency financial assistance for SORTA and Cincinnati Metro
items.sm: Urges Governor Mike DeWine and the Ohio Department of Transportation to provide emergency financial assistance to Ohio transit agencies, recognizing the severe financial impact of COVID-19 on SORTA and Cincinnati Metro.

items.t: Approve an alternative method of apportioning the Local Government Fund for 2021 through 2028
items.sm: Approves an alternative method of apportioning the undivided Local Government Fund under Section 5747.53 of the Ohio Revised Code for 2021 through 2028.

items.t: Express Council's will that members donate 10% of their salaries to the City
items.sm: Expresses the will of Council that all members donate 10% of their City salaries back to the City while City employees are on temporary emergency leave.

items.t: Authorize the transfer of $21,724 from the Clerk of Council budget to the General Fund
items.sm: Authorizes transferring $21,724, 10% of the remaining fiscal year 2020 Clerk of Council office budget, to the General Fund surplus because COVID-19 decreased revenues.

items.t: Amend the effective date of the Residential Rental Registration program
items.sm: Amends Section 874-13 of Chapter 874 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to allow time to implement the new program, given City service disruptions caused by the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.t: Amend the Municipal Code to hold City Council meetings on Wednesdays at 2:00 p.m
items.sm: Amends Section 101-3 of Chapter 101 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to provide that all City Council meetings are held on Wednesdays at 2:00 p.m.

items.t: Hold the first City Council meeting each month on Wednesdays at 2:00 p.m
items.sm: Asks Council to hold its first meeting of each month on Wednesdays at 2:00 p.m. and to amend the applicable Council Rule and Cincinnati Municipal Code provisions.

items.t: Accept and appropriate federal HOPWA funds, including COVID-19 funds, for 2020
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate $1,141,164 and an additional $145,186 in federal Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS funds to Fund 465 for 2020 projects.

items.t: Accept and appropriate federal Emergency Solutions Grant funds, including COVID-19 funds
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate $513,616 and an additional $769,056 in federal Emergency Solutions Grant funds to Emergency Shelter Fund 445 for 2020 projects.

items.t: Suspend Cincinnati Bell Streetcar operations for 90 days
items.sm: Asks the City to suspend Cincinnati Bell Streetcar operations for 90 days and asks the Health Commissioner to recommend best practices for the safety of riders on Metro buses and the Streetcar.

items.t: Provide dedicated Human Resources staffing for employees on Temporary Emergency Leave
items.sm: Asks the Administration to provide dedicated Human Resources Department staff, in adequate numbers, to assist City employees furloughed through the Temporary Emergency Leave process.

items.t: Change the meeting times of two Council committees
items.sm: Asks Council to move the Law & Public Safety Committee from Week A Monday to Week A Tuesday at 9 a.m. and the Economic Growth & Zoning Committee to 11 a.m.

items.t: Request cancellation of the April 8, 2020 City Council session
items.sm: Asks Council to cancel the April 8, 2020 Cincinnati City Council session.

items.t: Honor Peggy Brown for her contributions to education and family programs
items.sm: Recognizes and honors Peggy Brown for her accomplishments and contributions to education and family programs that help community members become self-sufficient.

items.t: Appoint Jan-Michele Lemon Kearney to City Council
items.sm: Designates Jan-Michele Lemon Kearney as successor to Councilmember Tamaya Dennard for the unexpired term ending January 4, 2022, under Article II, Section 4b of the City Charter.

items.t: Communication on the Hamilton County Sheriff's Office COVID-19 Outbreak Alternative Response Plan
items.sm: Submits a communication from the Hamilton County Sheriff's Department regarding the Hamilton County Sheriff's Office COVID-19 Outbreak Alternative Response Plan.

Request a report on the cost of family creation benefits
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report on the financial impact of offering $20,000 infertility coverage, a $20,000 adoption or surrogacy stipend and 6 weeks of parental leave at 100% pay.

items.t: Accept water main easements in Miami Township and vacate an easement section
items.sm: Accepts permanent water main easements from DRCC, LLC and Deer Run Neighborhood Association, Inc. in Miami Township and authorizes a Vacation Plat to vacate a section of a prior easement.

items.t: Authorize an application for a grant of up to $3,000,000 for Delhi-Fairbanks Safety Improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for up to $3,000,000 from the Ohio Department of Transportation's Highway Safety Improvement Program for the Delhi-Fairbanks Safety Improvements Project.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of a police canine donation from the Matt Haverkamp Foundation
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager and the Cincinnati Police Department to accept a canine worth $8,000 donated by the Matt Haverkamp Foundation.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of up to $370,000 in grants for Wasson Way Trail Phase 3
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate up to $370,000 from the Highway Safety Improvement Program for construction of Phase 3 of the Wasson Way Trail.

items.t: Reevaluate the recommended human service cuts
items.sm: Asks the Administration to reevaluate recommended human service cuts to food, housing, health and violence prevention organizations, and to avoid housing-related cuts such as eviction prevention.

items.t: Request racial and ethnic data in COVID-19 reporting and outreach to Black and Brown residents
items.sm: Asks that the City's COVID-19 information include racial and ethnic statistics and that the Cincinnati Health Department work with Interact for Health and the Center for Closing the Health Gap.

items.t: Establish an account and accept up to $20,000,000 in grants for Western Hills Viaduct
items.sm: Establishes a capital project account and authorizes the City Manager to accept up to $20,000,000 from ODOT's Local Major Bridge program for Western Hills Viaduct demolition, construction and a Duke Energy line relocation.

items.t: Authorize applying for FEMA reimbursement of COVID-19 response costs and establish Fund 477
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for and accept Federal Emergency Management Agency reimbursement for eligible COVID-19 costs and establishes Fund 477, FEMA 2020 COVID-19, to receive the funds.

items.t: Support reducing the African-American Chamber of Commerce's fiscal year 2020 funding by 25%
items.sm: Supports actions by the City Administration, working with the African-American Chamber of Commerce, to cut the Chamber's fiscal year 2020 General Fund allocation by at least 25 percent to fund essential services.

items.t: Support reducing third-party service provider funding by at least 25% for fiscal year 2020
items.sm: Supports City Administration actions to reduce fiscal year 2020 General Fund allocations to the City's third-party service providers by at least 25 percent to fund essential government services.

items.t: Authorize the vacation and sale of a portion of Monroe Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to vacate and sell a portion of Monroe Street in Walnut Hills to Fowler Street Investments, Ltd. for expansion of the adjacent business.

items.t: Department of Finance reports for the month ended February 29, 2020
items.sm: Submits the Department of Finance reports for the month ended February 29, 2020, from the City Manager.

items.t: Declare the necessity of assessing properties for special street lighting in Lighting Group 2
items.sm: Declares the necessity of assessing properties in Lighting Group 2 that benefit from special street lighting for the cost of the lighting for the three-year period beginning August 1, 2019.

items.t: Authorize accepting a $491,501 Ohio grant for opiate response and addiction treatment
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate up to $491,501 from the Ohio Department of Mental Health and Addictions Services for a media campaign, treatment, counseling, recovery supports and recovery housing.

items.t: Authorize a $100,000 federal grant for the Ohio River Security Camera Network
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $100,000 from the fiscal year 2020 Port Security Grant Program to maintain the Ohio River Security Camera Network.

items.t: Authorize state reimbursement of extradition costs for dangerous wanted offenders
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate reimbursement from the Ohio Office of Criminal Justice Services for in-state and out-of-state extradition costs, depositing the funds into the General Fund.

items.t: Explore shared service partnerships with the County and regional municipalities
items.sm: Asks the Administration, working with collective bargaining units, to bring Council one shared service opportunity with the County or other municipalities every 90 days and to form a working group.

items.t: Issue a local order on safety protections for frontline business workers
items.sm: Asks the Administration, with the Mayor and Health Commissioner, to issue a local order requiring daily staff screenings, protective equipment and safety and social distancing protocols for businesses.

items.t: Ask for an ordinance providing $500,000 in grants to minority-owned small businesses
items.sm: Asks the Administration to identify ways to help small businesses during COVID-19 and asks the Law Department to draft an ordinance repurposing $500,000 in unused Cincinnati Access Fund dollars as $5,000 to $20,000 grants.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of $2,726,172 in Emergency Solutions Grant funds for COVID-19 response
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate an additional $2,726,172 in federal Emergency Solutions Grant funds to Emergency Shelter Fund 445 to prevent, prepare for and respond to COVID-19.

items.t: Resume Zoning Hearing Examiner meetings online during the COVID-19 pandemic
items.sm: Asks the Administration to take steps to resume Zoning Hearing Examiner meetings, online if necessary, under Emergency Order 1 so development projects can continue.

items.t: Declare the necessity of assessing for the Urban Forestry Maintenance District in 2021
items.sm: Declares the necessity of assessing for the control of blight and disease of shade trees and for the planting, care, trimming and removal of shade trees in the Urban Forestry Maintenance District for 2021.

items.t: Communication from Bond Hill residents on the Quick Stop liquor license renewal
items.sm: Submits a communication from Bond Hill residents and Catalina Avenue homeowners regarding the renewal of the Quick Stop liquor license.

items.t: Support extending the 2020 liquor permit renewal deadline
items.sm: Expresses the City's support for extending the 2020 liquor permit renewal and fee payment deadline to 60 days after Ohio permit holders can sell alcoholic beverages for onsite consumption.

items.t: Request free parking meters and frozen penalties during the coronavirus emergency
items.sm: Asks the Administration to make parking meters free with no tickets through May 1, 2020, freeze penalties through May 15, 2020, and reschedule ticket hearings until after May 1.

items.t: Encourage FC Cincinnati to release the City from a $6,383,000 stadium infrastructure obligation
items.sm: Encourages FC Cincinnati to voluntarily release the City from its obligation to provide $6,383,000 for stadium infrastructure so the City can address potential capital budget shortfalls caused by COVID-19.

items.t: Presentation on Law and Public Safety crime statistics from the Cincinnati Police Department
items.sm: Presents Chief Eliot Isaac of the Cincinnati Police Department with a presentation titled Law and Public Safety Crime Statistics, submitted by Vice Mayor Smitherman.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of a donated $6,130 camera system for the Police Department
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept a Bounce Imaging Explorer camera system valued at $6,130 from the Matt Haverkamp Foundation for the Cincinnati Police Department.

items.t: Authorize an encroachment easement for Fulton Landing, LLC at 2062 Riverside Drive
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to grant Fulton Landing, LLC an encroachment easement for a building portion at 2062 Riverside Drive that encroaches on the Riverside Drive right-of-way in East End.

items.t: Authorize cooperation with the Ohio Department of Transportation on repairing two Gilbert Avenue bridges
items.sm: Authorizes the Administration to cooperate with the Ohio Department of Transportation to repair and rehabilitate two bridges along Gilbert Avenue, Seventh Street and Eighth Street over Eggleston Avenue.

items.t: Authorize cooperation with the Ohio Department of Transportation on repairing two Columbia Parkway bridges
items.sm: Authorizes the Administration to cooperate with the Ohio Department of Transportation to repair and rehabilitate two Columbia Parkway bridges over Heekin Avenue and the Eastern Avenue ramp.

items.t: Accept and appropriate a $10,000 Interact for Health grant for a COVID-19 quarantine facility
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate a $10,000 Interact for Health grant for food, gas and necessities at the Over-the-Rhine Recreation Center quarantine facility, depositing it into Public Health Research Fund 350.

items.t: Reallocate Community Development Block Grant funds for the Urgent Public Health Crisis Response Program
items.sm: Returns $1,584,150 to source and appropriates $1,376,271 within Community Development Block Grant Fund 304 for administration of the Urgent Public Health Crisis Response Program.

items.t: Establish the Hirsch Walking Trail project and accept a $360,000 grant
items.sm: Establishes a capital improvement project and authorizes accepting $360,000 from the Cincinnati Recreation Foundation to design and construct the one-third mile Hirsch Walking Trail at 3630 Reading Road in Avondale.

items.t: Report on the status of the Madison and Whetsel development
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report on the status of the Madison and Whetsel development, referencing Document No. 202000373.

items.t: Accept and appropriate $20,886 in additional federal HOPWA funds for COVID-19 response
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate an additional $20,886 in federal Housing Opportunities for Persons with AIDS funds to prevent, prepare for and respond to COVID-19.

items.t: Transfer $750,000 to convert Duke Energy Convention Center to a COVID-19 Alternate Care Site
items.sm: Authorizes transferring and appropriating $750,000 from the Convention Center Fund 103 surplus to convert and operate the Duke Energy Convention Center as a COVID-19 Alternate Care Site.

items.t: Accept a federal grant of up to $157,000 for Lunken Airport
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for and accept up to $157,000 in Federal Aviation Administration CARES Act funds to offset COVID-19 revenue losses and operating costs at Lunken Airport.

items.t: Apply for a $150,000 federal grant for missing individuals with dementia
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $150,000 from the U.S. Department of Justice to reduce injuries and deaths of missing individuals with dementia and developmental disabilities.

items.t: Modify Ordinance No. 337-2019 to delay the commercial waste definition's effective date
items.sm: Modifies Ordinance No. 337-2019 to move the effective date of the expanded commercial waste definition covering construction and demolition debris from January 1, 2020 to October 1, 2020.

items.t: Authorize grants and funding for the Little Duck Creek Bike Trail in Bramble Park
items.sm: Establishes a project account and authorizes up to $143,054 in Ohio Department of Natural Resources grant funds and a $47,684 match to build the Little Duck Creek Bike Trail in Madisonville.

items.t: Reallocate $910,122.05 in Home Investment Trust Fund 411 project accounts
items.sm: Returns to source and appropriates $910,122.05 among Home Investment Trust Fund 411 project accounts, announcing the City's intended use for the 2020 HOME Investment Partnerships Program projects.

items.t: Accept and appropriate a $257,339 federal grant for COVID-19 emergency response
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate a $257,339 grant from the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention for COVID-19 response, depositing it into Public Health Research Fund 350.

items.t: Report on parking system updates related to COVID-19
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report on updates to the City's parking system during the COVID-19 pandemic, referencing Document No. 202000485.

items.t: Expand the "First 10 Minutes Free" parking policy to all smart meters
items.sm: Asks the Parking Division of the Department of Community and Economic Development to extend the "First 10 Minutes Free" policy from the Central Business District to all smart parking meters in the City's 52 neighborhoods.

items.t: Accept and appropriate up to $100,000 from Interact for Health for emergency dental services
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate up to $100,000 from Interact for Health to retain dental staff for emergency dental services during COVID-19, using Public Health Research Fund 350.

items.t: Authorize encroachment easements for DMD Real Estate LLC at 1614 Hoffner Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to grant DMD Real Estate LLC encroachment easements for steps and landings at 1614 Hoffner Street encroaching on Hoffner Street and Gulow Street rights-of-way in Northside.

items.t: Move Budget and Finance Committee meetings to Wednesdays at 11:00 a.m. through May
items.sm: Asks Council to move the regular Budget and Finance Committee time from Mondays at 1:00 p.m. to Wednesdays at 11:00 a.m. of "A weeks" until the end of May.

items.lt: COMMUNICATION, submitted by Councilmember Mann from Wallace & Catherine Power, regarding Columbus Avenue Development.
items.t: COMMUNICATION, submitted by Councilmember Mann from Wallace & Catherine Power, regarding Columbus Avenue Development.
Request a report on permanently closing Eden Park's Twin Lakes area to vehicles
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report on the feasibility and advisability of permanently reserving the Twin Lakes area of Eden Park for pedestrians and cyclists, closed to vehicular through-traffic.

items.t: Authorize the vacation and sale of part of Nebraska Avenue to St. Joseph Cemetery Association
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to vacate and sell a portion of Nebraska Avenue in West Price Hill to the St. Joseph Cemetery Association for cemetery expansion.

items.t: Report on the cost of a new regional shooting range in Hamilton County
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report to Council on the cost of buying land and building a new regional shooting range in Hamilton County, including the cost of renting another range meanwhile.

items.t: Communication from Sue Wilke on public input at Council and committee meetings
items.sm: Submits a communication from Sue Wilke regarding public input and how it is handled for Council and committee meetings.

items.t: Prohibit employer retaliation against employees who stay home due to COVID-19
items.sm: Establishes on an emergency basis that employers may not retaliate against covered employees for obeying stay-at-home orders or staying home to care for a household member with COVID-19.

items.t: Expand enforcement options and penalties for public health order violations
items.sm: Modifies Chapters 1601-57 and 1601-59 and amends Sections 1501-8 and 1501-9 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to expand enforcement options and penalties for violating public health and safety orders.

items.t: Authorize cooperation with ODOT on guardrail replacement on local routes
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to cooperate with the Ohio Department of Transportation on replacing Type A anchor assembly guardrails on National Highway System local routes in Cincinnati.

items.t: Authorize an application for Ohio Transit Partnership Program funding
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager, on an emergency basis, to apply to the Ohio Department of Transportation for transit assistance under the Ohio Transit Partnership Program for state fiscal year 2021.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of donated rainbow flags for City Hall
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept rainbow flags, valued at about $160 each, from Councilmember Chris Seelbach to fly at City Hall during the Cincinnati Pride Parade and Festival.

items.t: Authorize an agreement with Wyoming and accept $90,000 for Millsdale Street
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to agree with the City of Wyoming on rehabilitating Millsdale Street from Woodbine Avenue to Burns Avenue and to accept and appropriate up to $90,000 from Wyoming.

items.t: Authorize a grant of up to $700,000 for Police Department innovation
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $700,000 from the U.S. Department of Justice to help the Cincinnati Police Department test and evaluate crime prevention practices and technology.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of a $330,000 donation for streetcar operations
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept up to $330,000 from CinciVTICA, LLC to support streetcar operations and maintenance, and transfers payments in lieu of taxes to the Streetcar Operations Fund.

items.t: Authorize acceptance of a $250,000 donation for Liberty Street safety improvements
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate a $250,000 donation from OTR Holdings Inc., a subsidiary of 3CDC, for the Liberty Street Safety Improvements project.

items.t: Report on the E-Scooter program Request for Proposals contracts
items.sm: Provides an update from the City Manager on the contracts resulting from the Request for Proposals for the E-Scooter program.

items.sm: Asks the Administration to report next week on how the City's purchasing power can help businesses and communities buy masks and hand sanitizer without using City money.

items.t: Communication from UFCW Local 75 on reducing COVID-19 exposure
items.sm: Communicates the position of UFCW Local 75 that the goal should be to eliminate exposure for workers and the public to the greatest extent possible.

items.t: Authorize applications to the Federal Transit Administration for streetcar funding
items.sm: Authorizes the filing of applications with the Federal Transit Administration for federal transportation assistance to fund the Cincinnati streetcar system.

items.t: Approve the Public Transportation Agency Safety Plan for the Cincinnati Bell Connector
items.sm: Approves the Public Transportation Agency Safety Plan for the Cincinnati Bell Connector, as recommended by the streetcar's Accountable Executive and Chief Safety Officer.

items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept an in-kind donation of a Juneteenth flag to fly at City Hall during June in recognition of Juneteenth as National Freedom Day.

items.t: Amend the Local Initiatives Support Corporation agreement to repurpose Cincinnati Access Fund dollars
items.sm: Asks the Administration to begin amending the 2019 Operations Agreement with the Local Initiatives Support Corporation so $500,000 in Cincinnati Access Fund dollars can fund grants to minority-owned small businesses.

items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate a $50,000 Greater Cincinnati Foundation grant for the Cincinnati Health Department to operate three emergency dental centers, depositing it into Public Health Research Fund 350.

items.t: Authorize a grant of up to $872,136 for coronavirus response
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $872,136 from the U.S. Department of Justice to help the City prevent, prepare for and respond to the coronavirus.

items.t: Report on Department of Finance reports for the month ended March 31, 2020
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report on the Department of Finance reports for the month ended March 31, 2020.

items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report on modifications and upgrades to aging infrastructure related to urban core redevelopment (see Document No. 201901841).

items.t: Authorize a Lunken Airport lease extension with Cin-Air Limited Partnership
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Lease Agreement with Cin-Air Limited Partnership extending its leasehold interest at Lunken Airport for up to an additional 20 years.

items.t: Authorize a Lunken Airport lease extension with Macy's Corporate Services, Inc
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Lease Agreement with Macy's Corporate Services, Inc. extending its leasehold interest at Lunken Airport for up to 5 years.

items.t: Encourage Ohio to extend temporary driver's licenses for one year
items.sm: Encourages the State of Ohio to extend temporary driver's licenses for one year because the closure of 52 driver examination locations during COVID-19 creates a road testing backlog for youth turning 16.

items.t: Encourage permanent driver's licenses for students leaving for military service
items.sm: Encourages the Governor and the Ohio General Assembly to let the Bureau of Motor Vehicles issue permanent driver's licenses to students with temporary licenses who are leaving for military service within six months.

items.t: Presentation on the pandemic's effects on Shelterhouse
items.sm: Presents Genell Stephens of Shelterhouse on the effects of the pandemic on Shelterhouse, submitted by Councilmember Seelbach.

items.t: Presentation on the pandemic's impact from the Center for Closing the Health Gap
items.sm: Presents Renee Mahaffey-Harris of the Center for Closing the Health Gap on the impact of the pandemic, submitted by Councilmember Seelbach.

items.t: Presentation on the effects of COVID-19 from Strategies to End Homelessness
items.sm: Presents Kevin Finn of Strategies to End Homelessness on the effects of COVID-19, submitted by Councilmember Seelbach.

items.t: Support flying a Juneteenth flag at City Hall in June
items.sm: Asks Council to support the Administration's plan to fly a Juneteenth flag at City Hall in June and to request an ordinance accepting a donated flag.

items.t: Establish a 15% cap on third-party food delivery fees charged to restaurants
items.sm: Establishes a cap of no more than 15% of the total food cost on fees third parties may charge Cincinnati restaurants for delivering food.

items.t: Establish a 15% cap on third-party restaurant food delivery fees
items.sm: Establishes a cap of no more than 15% of the total food cost on fees that third parties charge Cincinnati restaurants for delivery, and prohibits reducing delivery driver compensation because of the cap.

items.t: Report on JCTC Incentive Policy changes to the minimum qualifying wage
items.sm: Presents a report from the City Manager on changes to the minimum qualifying wage in the JCTC Incentive Policy.

items.t: Ask the Administration to raise the JCTC Minimum Qualifying Wage to $15
items.sm: Asks the Administration to amend the JCTC Minimum Qualifying Wage policy so that, beginning July 1, 2020, new JCTCs go only to businesses paying every position at least $15.

items.t: Presentation on the CCROW Unit and Victim's Assistance Liaison
items.sm: Presents Karen Rumsey of the Cincinnati Police Department on the CCROW Unit and the Victim's Assistance Liaison, submitted by Vice Mayor Smitherman.

items.t: Report on healthcare coverage and other subsidies
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's report regarding healthcare coverage and other subsidies.

items.t: Authorize transfers within the Restricted Funds and appropriate $447,637 for City departments
items.sm: Authorizes the transfer of $4,723,987 within the Restricted Funds and the appropriation of $447,637 from the unappropriated surplus to realign funds for the ongoing needs of City departments.

items.sm: Authorizes a $21,931 moral obligation payment to Public Allies, Inc. for hosting three Public Ally Members in the Office of Environment and Sustainability and the Office of Aging and Accessibility.

items.sm: Establishes the 2021 Urban Forestry Program Assessment Equalization Board, appoints three members to it and sets the time and place for hearings.

items.sm: Authorizes transferring $9,900,167 within the General Fund for City department needs and $200,000 to Towing Charges – Private Operators Fund 618 to cover a revenue shortfall.

items.sm: Authorizes the sale of City property at 1521 Vine Street and 1512-1520 Republic Street and a $1,000,000 HOME loan for about 56 residential units in Over-the-Rhine.

items.t: Traffic signal upgrades at Colerain Avenue and Virginia Avenue intersection
items.sm: Authorizes cooperation with Ohio DOT to upgrade traffic signals at Colerain Avenue and Virginia Avenue intersection.

items.sm: Adds Section 1101-87, "Diaper Changing Stations," to the Cincinnati Building Code to ensure equal access to diaper changing equipment regardless of gender in certain buildings with public toilet rooms.

items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate a $33,000 Greater Cincinnati Foundation grant to train health system staff to document patients' race and ethnicity during the COVID-19 pandemic.

items.sm: Amends Cincinnati Municipal Code Sections 513-7 and 869-7 to align vehicle impoundment fees and Police Rotation List rules with the fiscal year 2020 budget.

items.t: Authorize the labor management agreement with Teamsters Local 100
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute and implement the labor management agreement between the City of Cincinnati and Teamsters Local 100.

items.sm: Reports from the City Manager on converting all publicly accessible restrooms to touchless fixtures, in reference to document #202000469.

items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to amend the agreement with Madisonville Phase I, II and III LLCs and Ackermann Enterprises, and appropriates $950,000 from the Madisonville TIF District.

items.t: Authorize fare-free service on the Cincinnati Bell Connector streetcar (vetoed by the Mayor)
items.sm: Authorizes fare-free Cincinnati Bell Connector service beginning September 2, 2020, suspends streetcar fare requirements for 60 days and declares intent to legislate ongoing fare-free service; the Mayor vetoed it.

items.t: Reappoint Sandra Mosley to the Woodward High School Board of Trustees

items.sm: Mayor John Cranley reappoints Teri Spears to the Cincinnati Metropolitan Housing Authority Board of Commissioners for a term of five years, subject to Council's advice and consent.

items.sm: Mayor John Cranley reappoints Mark Childers to the Citizen Complaint Authority Board for a term of two years, subject to Council's advice and consent.

items.sm: Mayor John Cranley reappoints Dr. Joe N. Hackworth, MD to the Cincinnati Board of Health for a term of three years, subject to Council's advice and consent.

items.sm: Mayor John Cranley reappoints Ryan Dupree to the Board of the Hamilton County Community Action Agency for a term of three years, subject to Council's advice and consent.

items.t: Support legal action against the order limiting ballot drop boxes to one per county
items.sm: Opposes the Ohio Secretary of State's order limiting ballot drop boxes to one per county and supports legal action by the City Solicitor to ensure accessible drop boxes.

items.t: Request a report on homeownership programs and forgivable home repair loans
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report within 14 days on programs promoting low-income homeownership, the feasibility of forgivable repair loans, and funding sources for repairs repaid on a sliding scale.

items.t: Request an end to adding code enforcement fines to property tax bills
items.sm: Asks the Administration to stop adding code enforcement fines to residential property tax bills and to recommend within 14 days a program like the former Harbor Fund.

items.t: Amend the registration information required of residential rental property owners
items.sm: Amends Section 874-5 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code to modify the registration information required of residential rental property owners, addressing business operators' privacy concerns as the city-wide rental registration program is implemented.

items.t: Recognize March as Reading Awareness Month
items.sm: Recognizes March as Reading Awareness Month and promotes the benefits of reading in Cincinnati by joining with local literacy organizations, schools, the library and Cincinnati Children's Hospital Medical Center.

items.t: Request a report on enforcement of short term rental nuisance provisions
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report on enforcement of Section 865-15 limits on short term rental occupancy and criminal activity, including suspensions or revocations under Section 865-25 and recommendations for better enforcement.

items.t: Urge Ohio's Congressional members to reverse reduced post office services
items.sm: Urges Senators Sherrod Brown and Rob Portman and Representatives Steve Chabot and Brad Wenstrup to reverse the Postmaster General's decision to reduce services in post office branches.

items.t: Give Dana Avenue the honorary name William J. Keating Way
items.sm: Declares that Dana Avenue between Victory Parkway and Madison Road receives the honorary secondary name William J. Keating Way in memory of William J. Keating.

items.t: Express Council's belief that the Cincinnati Bell Connector's success is the City's responsibility
items.sm: Expresses Council's belief that the Administration, the Mayor and Council are responsible for the Cincinnati Bell Connector's success and encourages steps to safeguard the taxpayers' investment in it.

items.t: Support the creation of Transportation Development Districts in Ohio
items.sm: Urges the Ohio General Assembly to pass legislation enabling Transportation Development Districts that could fund, plan, build and maintain transportation-related projects.

items.action: Referred to Law & Public Safety Committee
items.t: Urge removal of the involuntary servitude exception for convicted persons from constitutions
items.sm: Urges the Ohio General Assembly and the United States Congress to remove the involuntary servitude phrase from the United States Constitution and from Article 1, Section 6 of the Ohio Constitution.

items.t: Support investment in the reopened Findlay Playground
items.sm: Asks Council to support and commit to investing in Findlay Playground, including Downtown/OTR TIF funds, a steering committee and an agreement between the Cincinnati Recreation Commission and a development manager.

items.t: Request a report on a stop sign on Heekin Avenue near Bouton Street
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report on the feasibility of a stop sign on Heekin Avenue near Bouton Street in Linwood and to recommend a safe solution for speeding and collisions.

items.t: Request a report on a Parklet Program for restaurant outdoor dining
items.sm: Asks the Administration to report on the feasibility of a Parklet Program using City-controlled right of way, with local businesses owning and operating parklets and the City collecting revenue.

items.t: Support funding for the United States Postal Service and oppose removing postal boxes
items.sm: Expresses Council's belief that Congress must fund the United States Postal Service, that Postmaster General Louis DeJoy must reverse delay-causing directives, and opposes removing postal boxes from Cincinnati.

items.sm: Establishes the Economic Development Reform Panel to study the City's development process and transfers $100,000 from the General Fund reserve to the City Manager's Office to implement it.

items.t: Authorize a utility easement for the University of Cincinnati on Clifton Avenue
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Grant of Easement to the Board of Trustees of the University of Cincinnati across City-owned Clifton Avenue right-of-way in CUF.

items.t: Accept a $32,500 Cincinnati Fire Foundation donation for EMS Mountain Bike Unit equipment
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept up to $32,500 from the Cincinnati Fire Foundation and appropriate it for advanced life support equipment for the Cincinnati Fire Department's EMS Mountain Bike Unit.

items.t: Establish the LeBlond Walking Trail Grant project and accept a $70,000 grant
items.sm: Establishes the LeBlond Walking Trail Grant project and authorizes accepting up to $70,000 from the Land and Water Conservation Fund for a 0.25 mile trail connecting LeBlond Playground and St. Rose Soccer Field.

items.t: Authorize a utility easement for Duke Energy Ohio at 7215 Bridgetown Road
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Grant of Easement in favor of Duke Energy Ohio, Inc. over City-owned property at 7215 Bridgetown Road in Miami Township.

items.t: Authorize a Fourth Amendment to the Warren County water area contract
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Fourth Amendment to the water area contract with the Warren County Board of County Commissioners, modifying the area the City serves.

items.t: Designate Bellevue Avenue in Corryville as a Residential Parking Permit Area
items.sm: Designates Bellevue Avenue from William H. Taft Road to Oak Street as a Residential Parking Permit Area, limiting parking to permit holders from 7 a.m. to 10 p.m., Monday through Saturday.

items.t: Accept donated property on Auburn Avenue and East McMillan Street for right-of-way
items.sm: Accepts land donated by Auburn Land Holdings LLC and 45 WHT LLC along Auburn Avenue and East McMillan Street for dedication as public right-of-way for road improvements.

items.t: Designate a Residential Parking Permit Area on Green Street and Republic Street
items.sm: Designates portions of Green Street from Race to Vine Street and Republic Street from East Elder to Liberty Street in Over-the-Rhine as a Residential Parking Permit Area.

items.t: Authorize a Fourth Amendment to the contract with the City of Reading, Ohio
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Fourth Amendment to the contract between the City of Cincinnati and the City of Reading, Ohio.

items.t: Authorize a sixth amendment to the water contract with the Village of Addyston
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Sixth Amendment to the Water Contract between the City of Cincinnati and the Village of Addyston, Ohio.

items.t: Authorize a water service agreement with the City of Wyoming for standby water
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Water Service Agreement with the City of Wyoming, Ohio for the continued sale of standby water.

items.t: Authorize a third amendment to the water service contract with the Village of Glendale
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Third Amendment to the Water Service Contract between the City of Cincinnati and the Village of Glendale, Ohio.

items.t: Authorize a second amendment to the water service agreement with the Village of Woodlawn
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute a Second Amendment to the water service Agreement between the City of Cincinnati and the Village of Woodlawn, Ohio.

items.t: Establish a $2,000,000 project for outdoor dining and streetscape improvements in three neighborhoods
items.sm: Establishes a capital project account and transfers and appropriates $2,000,000 from the Downtown/OTR East TIF District fund for outdoor dining and pedestrian safety improvements in the Central Business District, Over-the-Rhine and Pendleton.

items.t: Report on the Finance and Budget Monitoring Report for the period ending October 31, 2020
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's Finance and Budget Monitoring Report for the period ending October 31, 2020.

items.t: Authorize a grant of up to $78,248.94 for free Wi-Fi at nature centers
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for and accept up to $78,248.94 from the Hamilton County CARES Expanding Free Wi-Fi Program to expand Wi-Fi at nature centers and the Krohn Conservatory.

items.t: Authorize capital budget transfers and new project accounts for the Capital Improvement Program
items.sm: Authorizes four new capital project accounts, a $1,982.98 redirection of donated funds, and transfers among general and restricted capital funds to carry out the Capital Improvement Program.

items.t: Accept and appropriate Hamilton County Coronavirus Relief Fund money for COVID-19 expenses
items.sm: Authorizes accepting and appropriating Hamilton County Coronavirus Relief Fund money, including $1,000,000 for the Duke Energy Convention Center and $621,787.66 for the Over-the-Rhine Recreation Center isolation facility.

items.t: Establish a $230,000 project to replace the USquare Garage parking system
items.sm: Establishes a capital project and transfers and appropriates $230,000 from the Parking System Facilities Fund to replace the parking access and revenue control system at the USquare Garage East and West.

items.t: Authorize the transfer of $600,000 among General Capital Budget project accounts
items.sm: Authorizes returning $600,000 from various capital improvement program project accounts to Capital Funds 858 and 870 and appropriating it to an existing project account, per the attached Schedule of Transfer.

items.t: Authorize donations to rename Reading Road as President Barack Obama Avenue
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to solicit, accept and deposit donations into Fund 314, Special Events, to rename the stretch of Reading Road within Cincinnati as President Barack Obama Avenue.

items.t: Accept a $50,000 donation for the Bengals DIVE RIGHT Flag Football Program
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept and appropriate a $50,000 donation from the Cincinnati Recreation Foundation, on behalf of the Cincinnati Bengals, to deliver the DIVE RIGHT Flag Football Program to area youth.

items.t: Accept up to $3,475,670 in grants for Phases 4 and 5 of the Wasson Way Trail
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept up to $3,475,670 in federal grants for Wasson Way Trail Phases 4 and 5 and to enter a Local Public Agency agreement with the Ohio Department of Transportation.

items.t: Accept a $75,000 grant for youth programming during the COVID-19 pandemic
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to apply for, accept and appropriate up to $75,000 from the Hamilton County CARES Youth Services Relief Fund to help the Cincinnati Recreation Department with increased youth programming costs.

items.t: Accept a $126,500 grant for the Red Bank Expressway rehabilitation in Madisonville
items.sm: Establishes a project account and authorizes the City Manager to accept up to $126,500 from the Hamilton County Municipal Road Fund to rehabilitate a portion of Red Bank Expressway in Madisonville.

items.t: Rename the Parks Private Endowment fund and accept a $6,500 donation
items.sm: Amends Ordinance No. 324-2018 to rename Fund 430 the Parks Private Endowment and Donations fund and accepts up to $6,500 from the Cincinnati Off-Road Alliance for Mt. Airy Bike Skills Park design.

items.t: Appropriate $5,724,193.76 from the Income Tax-Transit Fund to SORTA
items.sm: Appropriates $5,724,193.76 from the unappropriated surplus of Fund 759 to the Southwest Ohio Regional Transit Authority to implement Ordinance No. 0247-2020 and the amended 1973 City-SORTA Agreement.

items.t: Establish the Recycling Operations Technician classification and salary range
items.sm: Establishes the classification and salary range schedule for the new Recycling Operations Technician position and enacts Section 322 of Division 0, Chapter 307 of the Cincinnati Municipal Code.

items.t: Accept in-kind donations worth up to $14,581.45 from the Cincinnati Parks Foundation
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to accept in-kind donations of park supplies, personal protective equipment and pickle ball equipment valued at up to $14,581.45 from the Cincinnati Parks Foundation for various City parks.

items.t: Authorize a $639,488.64 payment to Keep Cincinnati Beautiful as a moral obligation
items.sm: Authorizes the payment of $639,488.64 from various operating accounts to Keep Cincinnati Beautiful for litter prevention, recycling and community improvement services provided to the City.

items.t: Amend Ordinance No. 256-2019 to fund Imagination Alley infrastructure improvements
items.sm: Amends Ordinance No. 256-2019 to provide $500,000 of the $1,850,000 appropriated for public infrastructure in Imagination Alley, in addition to Vine, Fifteenth and Race Street improvements in Over-the-Rhine.

items.t: Authorize accepting up to $10,000,000 from the Hamilton County Coronavirus Relief Fund
items.sm: Authorizes the City to accept up to $10,000,000 from the Hamilton County Coronavirus Relief Fund and appropriate it to reimburse Cincinnati Fire Department personnel costs for the COVID-19 response.

items.t: Authorize labor agreements with the Fraternal Order of Police, Local 69
items.sm: Authorizes the City Manager to execute and implement the Non-Supervisors and Supervisors labor management agreements between the City and the Fraternal Order of Police, Local 69.

items.t: Report on finance and budget monitoring for the period ending September 30, 2020
items.sm: Presents the City Manager's Finance and Budget Monitoring Report for the period ending September 30, 2020.

items.t: Authorize cooperation with the Ohio Department of Transportation on two Martin Drive bridges
items.sm: Authorizes the Administration to cooperate with the Ohio Department of Transportation to repair and rehabilitate two Martin Drive bridges over Columbia Parkway in Mt. Adams.

items.t: Appoint Councilmember Goodin to three Council committees
items.sm: Asks Council to appoint Councilmember Steven P. Goodin to the Budget and Finance, Economic Growth and Zoning, and Law and Public Safety Committees.

meetings.body: Equity, Inclusion, Youth, & The Arts Committee
